events.title: Declaration of Independence Adopted
events.description: The Second Continental Congress, meeting in Philadelphia, approved the final wording of the Declaration of Independence. The document announced that the thirteen American colonies regarded themselves as free and independent states, no longer under British rule.
events.significance: The date became the United States' national holiday, Independence Day. The Declaration's ideas about liberty and self-government have influenced independence and rights movements around the world.

events.title: Jefferson and Adams Die on the Nation's 50th Anniversary
events.description: Thomas Jefferson, the principal author of the Declaration of Independence, died at Monticello. Later that same day John Adams died in Massachusetts, exactly fifty years after the Declaration was adopted.
events.significance: The deaths of two Founding Fathers on the Jubilee of American independence struck many Americans as providential. They marked the passing of the Revolutionary generation.

events.title: Confederate Surrender at Vicksburg
events.description: After a siege of more than six weeks, Confederate General John C. Pemberton surrendered Vicksburg, Mississippi, to Union General Ulysses S. Grant. The surrender came one day after the Union victory at Gettysburg.
events.significance: The Union gained control of the Mississippi River and split the Confederacy in two. Together with Gettysburg, the victory is widely seen as a turning point of the Civil War.

events.title: Marie Curie Dies
events.description: Marie Curie, the Polish-born physicist and chemist, died in France at age 66 of aplastic anemia, most likely caused by her years of exposure to radiation. She had pioneered research into radioactivity and discovered the elements polonium and radium.
events.significance: Curie was the first woman to win a Nobel Prize and remains the only person to win Nobel Prizes in two different sciences. Her work laid the foundations for modern nuclear physics and cancer treatment.

events.title: Mars Pathfinder Lands on Mars
events.description: NASA's Mars Pathfinder spacecraft landed on the Red Planet, using airbags to cushion its touchdown. It deployed Sojourner, a small rover that began exploring the surface.
events.significance: Sojourner was the first wheeled rover to operate on Mars. The mission showed that low-cost robotic exploration was feasible and paved the way for later rovers such as Spirit, Opportunity, Curiosity, and Perseverance.
